4. The Question on the Forest “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘five qualities of the forest should be adopted,’ what are those five qualities that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, that which is called a forest conceals impure people;”
In the same way, Great King, a yogi practicing yoga should conceal the transgressions and lapses of others and not expose them.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the forest that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, a forest is empty of crowds of people.
In the same way, Great King, the yogin practicing yoga must be empty of the net of lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, and views, as well as of all defilements.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the forest that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the forest is secluded and free from the crowding of people.
In the same way, great king, a yogin who is a practitioner of yoga must remain secluded from evil, unwholesome, and ignoble states.
This, great king, is the third quality of the forest that should be adopted.
Furthermore, great king, the forest is peaceful and pure.
In the same way, great king, a practitioner of yoga, a follower of yoga, should be peaceful, pure, extinguished, free from conceit, and free from malice.
This, great king, is the fourth quality of the forest that should be adopted.
Furthermore, great king, the forest is frequented by noble persons.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga should be one who is frequented by noble persons.
This, Great King, is the fifth quality of the forest that should be adopted.
And this, Great King, was spoken by the Blessed One, the God above gods, in the excellent Saṃyutta Nikāya:
With noble ones who live in seclusion,
who are resolute and meditative,
and who have constantly aroused their energy.
"One should dwell with the wise.
This is the fourth question of Pavanaṅga.
